situation: My dog Rufus died last Tuesday and the house is too quiet without his collar jingling in the hall.
poem:
The jingle is gone out of the front hall,
and Rufus is a shape the dusk keeps.
His collar hangs and does not say a word.
The house has learned a colder kind of quiet.

situation: The letter came today: I have been accepted to the marine biology program in Bergen.
poem:
Bergen! and the letter warm in your two hands,
the cold blue north unlatching all its doors.
You will go down among the green sea-rooms,
and come up salted, glittering, and changed.

situation: My mother's biopsy results come back on Friday and I have cleaned the kitchen three times.
poem:
The kitchen shines; it cannot shine enough.
Friday sits in the corner like a stone.
You scrub the same clean tile a third time,
and the clock will not be hurried on.

situation: I have been waiting at the DMV in chair forty-two for two hours and my number still has not been called.
poem:
Chair forty-two, and the hour gone soft and grey,
a voice calls numbers, none of them your own.
The strip-lights hum their one long yellow note.
O patience, O the slow varnish of waiting.

situation: My landlord kept my whole deposit for one scuff on the baseboard and will not answer his phone.
poem:
A scuff no wider than a thumb, and he keeps all,
your deposit swallowed, and the phone gone dumb.
Write the letter. Take him to the small court.
The red of it will keep you warm tonight.

situation: The tornado passed two streets over and our oak tree is still standing.
poem:
The black wind went by on the next street,
and our oak stands, ragged and holding on.
Green light after; the air rinsed and sweet.
We count the leaves and find them all.

situation: I burned the first pancake again, the way my grandmother always did, and the smoke alarm went off.
poem:
Black as your grandmother's first one, every time,
the pancake goes into the bin, unmourned.
The alarm shrills gold above the blue gas,
and the next one rises perfect and round.

situation: My daughter Maya took her first steps across the kitchen tile this morning, straight into the dog's water bowl.
poem:
She lets go of the chair and simply goes,
Maya, three steps, four, then water everywhere.
The dog's bowl breaks into a hundred suns,
and the tile is loud with her small triumph.

situation: I sold my father's blue Volvo yesterday and forgot to take the pine air freshener off the mirror.
poem:
The blue Volvo turns the corner and is gone,
the pine tree swinging still beneath the mirror.
You meant to take it. You did not.
Your father's evening goes off down the road.

situation: I have to give a toast at my brother's wedding on Saturday and I have rewritten it eleven times.
poem:
Eleven times the same words torn and written,
and Saturday arriving with its white noise.
Your brother is not the judge you fear;
the glass will shake, and no one minds.

situation: It has rained for six days and I have reread the same page of my library book four times.
poem:
Six days, and the rain keeps its one word.
The page holds still; the eye slides off.
Grey on grey on grey, and the gutters singing,
and the book asleep across your two knees.

situation: Someone keyed my car in the grocery store lot while I was inside buying milk.
poem:
Milk in the bag, and a scar on the door,
white and long and dug by a stranger's hand.
The lot goes on with its flat grey humming,
and something in your chest turns hot and sharp.

situation: My flight from Denver landed twenty minutes before the blizzard closed the runway. I have never been so glad to see a jetway.
poem:
The wheels touched, and twenty minutes later, nothing,
the runway white and closed as a shut eye.
You are down. You are inside. You are warm.
Denver goes on snowing without you now.

situation: I found a five dollar bill in my winter coat pocket along with a movie ticket from last February.
poem:
Something forgotten turns up in the dark,
small and bright as a coin of old sun.
The year gives back a little of itself,
and the ordinary hour is briefly gold.

situation: My best friend Priya moved to Auckland on Sunday and we finished the last of the chili in her freezer.
poem:
The last bowl of chili, and then the door,
and Priya gone the whole width of the world.
Auckland holds her now in its bright morning,
and the freezer hums where her winter was.

situation: After eleven months of looking, I start the new job at the bakery on Monday.
poem:
Eleven months of no, and now a yes,
warm as the oven mouth on Monday morning.
Flour will settle in the creases of your hands,
and the long waiting goes out like steam.

situation: My son has not texted back in three days and his last message was just a period.
poem:
Three days of nothing after that small dot,
that period sitting like a closed grey door.
You read it twenty times; it will not open.
The phone is heavy with all he has not said.

situation: I finally fixed the squeaking gate with a bit of olive oil because I could not find the WD-40.
poem:
Olive oil where the WD-40 should have been,
and the gate gives up its long thin cry.
It swings now smooth as oil on still water,
and the afternoon is one squeak lighter.

situation: My coworker Dan presented my spreadsheet in the Tuesday meeting and never once said my name.
poem:
Dan reads your rows aloud and takes the room,
your name left out like a dropped stitch.
The spreadsheet wears his voice, not yours,
and the meeting moves on, and you burn.

situation: The cat came back after four nights out, thin and loud, and slept twelve hours on my sweater.
poem:
Four nights, and then the yowl at the door,
thin as a wire and loud as a bell.
He sleeps the clock twice round on your sweater,
and the house lets out its long held breath.
